headline: Two online stores grew purchase volume in a single quarter while keeping return on ad spend high.
context: Two fashion and beauty brands selling through their own online stores in Egypt, with Meta as the paid channel for the campaign period.
objective: Grow online purchase volume quickly for both stores without letting return on ad spend fall as budgets rose.
challenge: Scaling spend quickly usually lowers the return on each additional pound. The plan had to grow volume without that drop.
strategy: Concentrate budget on middle- and bottom-of-funnel audiences with purchase intent, and build creative to be tested rather than simply published.
execution: Twelve Meta campaigns on the larger account. Budget was moved daily toward the ad sets producing purchases and away from those that were not.
outcome: Account A returned 13.84× on EGP 535K of spend across 82 days; account B returned 8.91×.
note: ROAS and purchase value are Meta-attributed.

period: Aug – early Oct 2024 · Saudi National Day
headline: A crowded national season, driven by product offers rather than deep discounts.
context: A Saudi furniture and décor retailer selling online, going into Saudi National Day, one of the busiest and most discount-heavy retail periods of the year.
objective: Raise return on ad spend from 4 to 7 over the National Day season, without relying on deep discounts.
challenge: Competitors were running much larger discounts, and the plan ruled out both heavy discounting and influencers, keeping the budget for the ad platforms themselves.
strategy: Win on product, not price: introduce new hero products, rearrange the online store around high-demand items, and pair high-value pieces with complementary lower-priced ones to raise basket value. Discounts stayed under 20%, and the budget was weighted 90/10 toward conversion over awareness.
execution: Campaigns started in August, ahead of the season, across Google, Instagram and Snapchat, with targeted abandoned-cart retargeting. Daily monitoring and adjustments kept campaigns out of the learning phase through National Day and into early October.
outcome: Return on ad spend rose from 4 to 10, against a target of 7. The store recorded SAR 1.09M in sales over the period from a SAR 100K media budget (Google 40K, Instagram 40K, Snapchat 20K): 507 orders, 15–20 a day, with 446 first-time customers.
note: Store sales are total sales for the period from the store platform, not only sales attributed to ads.

source.en: Agency case study, with the store platform’s sales dashboard for the period
source.ar: دراسة حالة من الوكالة، مع لوحة مبيعات منصة المتجر للفترة

measured.en: ROAS as reported in the case study (4 at the start, 10 at the end, against a target of 7). Total store sales, orders and new customers from the store platform’s dashboard, set against the total media budget.
measured.ar: العائد كما ورد في دراسة الحالة (4 في البداية و10 في النهاية مقابل مستهدف 7). وإجمالي مبيعات المتجر والطلبات والعملاء الجدد من لوحة منصة المتجر، مقابل إجمالي الميزانية الإعلانية.

open.en: Client approval to publish; the ad-platform export confirming ROAS; confirmation of the 2024 campaign year.
open.ar: موافقة العميل على النشر؛ وملف المنصات الإعلانية الذي يؤكد العائد؛ وتأكيد أن الحملة كانت في 2024.

headline: Every Ramadan series in one place, sponsored by one bank.
context: QNB Al Ahli wanted to promote m.visa, its mobile payment service, during Ramadan, when audiences in Egypt gather around the season’s TV series.
objective: Build awareness and traffic for the bank’s m.visa service during Ramadan.
challenge: Sponsorship of individual Ramadan series was sold out, and priced far above the budget.
strategy: Instead of sponsoring one series, own the whole category: a single destination for every Ramadan series, carrying the bank’s name.
execution: A partnership with the entertainment portal Filfan to build “Ramadan Series Sponsored by QNB”, with traffic driven to it from FilGoal, Facebook and Google Display.
outcome: 7M video views, 25M impressions and 50K clicks through to m.visa over Ramadan 2015.
note: Awareness and traffic metrics. No sales figures are claimed for this campaign.

headline: High-value homes sold through paid social, optimised for buyers rather than leads.
context: An Omani real estate developer selling high-value residential units.
objective: Sell high-value residential units through paid social.
challenge: Reach buyers ready to commit to a high-value purchase — not just people willing to leave a phone number.
strategy: Judge the campaign by units sold rather than by cost per lead.
outcome: 13 units sold and $1.51M in revenue from $18.2K of ad spend.

measured.en: Value of units sold to buyers who came through the campaign, against ad spend.
measured.ar: قيمة الوحدات المباعة لمشترين جاؤوا عبر الحملة، مقابل الإنفاق الإعلاني.

open.en: Campaign period; how sales were matched to campaign leads; client approval.
open.ar: فترة الحملة؛ وطريقة ربط المبيعات بعملاء الحملة؛ وموافقة العميل.

headline: A high-ticket peak season built on purchase intent, not volume.
context: An Egyptian online retailer of high-ticket electronics, going into the fourth-quarter peak season.
objective: Grow high-value orders through the Q4 peak season.
challenge: High-ticket products, a minimal budget and the busiest season of the year.
strategy: Spend only where purchase intent was already visible: middle- and bottom-of-funnel audiences.
execution: Meta campaigns focused on middle- and bottom-of-funnel audiences throughout the season.
outcome: $897K in Meta-attributed purchase value from 747 orders, at $1,201 per order.
note: Meta-attributed. The platform-reported ROAS for this period is not shown until it is confirmed from the original export.

source.en: Meta Ads Manager report in the campaign deck
source.ar: تقرير Meta Ads Manager في ملف الحملة

measured.en: Meta-attributed purchase value and purchases; average order value = value ÷ purchases.
measured.ar: قيمة المشتريات وعددها كما تنسبها Meta؛ متوسط الطلب = القيمة ÷ عدد المشتريات.

open.en: Original Ads Manager export; client approval.
open.ar: ملف Ads Manager الأصلي؛ وموافقة العميل.

headline: An offline retailer’s return on ad spend doubled within two weeks of launching online.
context: An established offline retailer moving into online sales for the first time.
objective: Launch online sales for an established offline retailer and improve return on ad spend quickly.
challenge: No online sales history to learn from, so early decisions had to be made on very little data.
strategy: Run for conversion from day one, and let early purchase data decide where the budget goes.
execution: Conversion campaigns on Meta and Google.
outcome: ROAS rose from 2× to 4× within two weeks, across 2,970 purchases.

measured.en: Platform-reported ROAS at launch compared with ROAS after two weeks.
measured.ar: العائد المُبلّغ من المنصات عند الإطلاق مقارنة بالعائد بعد أسبوعين.

open.en: Market, year and platform export; client approval.
open.ar: السوق والسنة وملف المنصة؛ وموافقة العميل.

headline: Qualified leads for a limited-time offer, at a low cost per lead.
context: DAMAC was marketing a limited-time offer on residences at Paramount Tower in the UAE.
objective: Generate qualified buyer leads for a limited-time Paramount Tower offer.
challenge: A short offer window, where lead quality mattered more than volume.
strategy: Tune lead-generation campaigns for qualification rather than raw lead count.
execution: Lead-generation campaigns on Meta for the offer period.
outcome: Leads at $8 each, with 15% qualifying as genuine prospects.

measured.en: Cost per lead and the share of leads that qualified, as stated in the case study.
measured.ar: تكلفة العميل ونسبة العملاء المؤهلين، كما وردت في دراسة الحالة.

open.en: Period, lead volume and baseline; permission to name DAMAC.
open.ar: الفترة وعدد العملاء وخط الأساس؛ وإذن ذكر اسم داماك.
